"Attacks" probably refers to denial of service attempts, fake requests that just suck up resources so the site won't load for real users. A defense would be designing a response system that can either deliver more responses than the attacker is able to fake-request, or being smart enough to not even respond to certain patterns so that resources stay available for the real intended users.

It's very tricky to fine tune, you can ignore certain ip addresses, user agents, cookies, browsers, etc. But the problem is every time you block something, you risk blocking real users by accident. And if the attacker realizes they've been blocked, they can change their patterns.
